source.title: Asymptotic Theory of Iterated Empirical Risk Minimization, with Applications to Active Learning

page_placements.theme: Intermediate optima in staged data or computation budgets

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses classical double descent and reports its own selection-driven error curve, but does not test any listed version's model-size, epoch, sample-count, general-capacity, effective-complexity, noise/regularization, or parameter-count claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites classical double-descent work, but cited results are not rows. Its own double-descent result varies the composition of the selected training set via the first-stage budget fraction ψ while model size and total labeled sample count are fixed; this does not measure V1–V7. Fig. 2 reports a U-shaped curve over ψ on a real dataset, also not one of the listed axes.
record.test_reason: The study's own double-descent curve is over the first-stage budget fraction ψ, with model dimension d and total labeled sample count γn held fixed. None of V1–V7's axes are varied: model size, epochs, total samples, capacity across model classes, an effective-complexity measure, noise or regularization tuning, or parameter recounting. The authors present this as distinct from classical size- or sample-driven double descent. Prior double-descent work is only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a double descent in test error as a function of budget allocation ψ, at fixed model and sample size, driven by the composition of the selected set. They attribute the peak near ψ=1/α to the base classifier overfitting and biasing selection. They also report an optimal-allocation tradeoff (U-shape), confirmed on chest X-ray data.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes two-stage ERM and active-learning data selection, varying budget allocation and selected-set composition; it does not use the original model-size, epoch, or sample-count sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with budget fraction ψ and total budget γ; the paper also compares small-margin versus large-margin selection, oracle access, and reusing versus holding out the first-stage data.

fits_no_version.finding: For linear classifiers at fixed d and fixed total labeled samples γn, test error versus first-stage budget fraction ψ shows a double-descent shape. The peak lies near ψ=1/α, where the base classifier's own training set is about d samples and it overfits, biasing selection. Theory matches simulations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In two-stage active learning, double descent in final test error can arise from the base classifier's interpolation threshold propagating through data selection, at fixed final model size and sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: On pneumonia chest X-ray (scattering features, logistic regression, α=5.41), test error versus ψ is U-shaped for γ = 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Budget allocation between base and final classifier yields a U-shaped test-error curve on real active-learning data.

record.problems: The relevant curves are presented in figures rather than tabulated values. Fig. 1's prose says numerical experiments use d=1000, while its caption says d=2000. The results are for linear classifiers and budget allocation, not the versions' model-size, epoch, or sample-count sweeps.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were left out.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep in deep networks.
No test error over training epochs.
Total labeled sample count is fixed along each curve. The Appendix G pruning figures vary α but test pruning policies, not more-data-hurts near a threshold.
No capacity sweep past an interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure is defined or used to predict peak location.
Regularization is fixed (λ=0.01). Label noise appears only in the pruning example, without a double-descent analysis. The authors flag optimized λ as future work.

record.verdict_notes: The peak location ψ≈1/α equals the first-stage interpolation threshold (ψn = d). This is an indirect link to sample-wise double descent of the base estimator, but final error at fixed total samples is not a V3 or V5 test. All relevant results are figure-only. Appendix G pruning results (less data can beat the full dataset) are about selection, not near-threshold more-data-hurts.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and peak near the training-set interpolation threshold.
Test error over training epochs or training time.
Changing sample count near an interpolation threshold.
Capacity sweeps across model classes past an interpolation point.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.
Whether noise or variance drives the peak, whether it splits into multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes it.
Recounting complexity by effective parameters and testing whether this makes the curve an ordinary U-shape.
